content: CD160 antigen is a protein encoded by the CD160 gene in humans. It is a 27 kDa glycoprotein that was initially identified using the monoclonal antibody BY55. The expression of CD160 is closely associated with peripheral blood natural killer (NK) cells and CD8+ T lymphocytes that exhibit cytolytic effector activity. The cDNA sequence of CD160 predicts a cysteine-rich, glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored protein composed of 181 amino acids. This protein contains a single immunoglobulin (Ig)-like domain that shows weak homology to the KIR2DL4 molecule. On the cell surface, CD160 is expressed as a tightly disulfide-linked multimer. The expression of CD160 is highly restricted to circulating NK and T cells, as well as to the spleen and small intestine. Within NK cells, CD160 is expressed by CD56dimCD16+ cells. Among circulating T cells, its expression is primarily limited to TCRγδ-bearing cells and to TCRαβ+CD8brightCD95+CD56+CD28−CD27− cells. In tissues, CD160 is expressed on all intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes. It demonstrates broad specificity for binding to both classical and non-classical MHC class I molecules. Clinical Significance CD160 serves as a ligand for HVEM (herpesvirus entry mediator) and is considered a proposed immune checkpoint inhibitor with anti-cancer activity, particularly in conjunction with anti-PD-1 antibodies. Additionally, CD160 has been suggested as a potential new therapeutic target in cases of human pathological ocular and tumor neovascularization that are unresponsive or resistant to existing anti-angiogenic drugs.
